headline: Elon Musk replied "Yikes" to a chart of CoreWeave's borrowing costs near 15%, and CoreWeave shares fell 15% on Wednesday.
score_reason: Pool score kept: market-moving AI credit story with named voices; the share fall is a fact, the bubble claim is an opinion.
importance_line: A bond yield near 15% means lenders want a steep return to lend to CoreWeave, which matters to its investors, to other AI cloud companies whose shares also fell, and to any AI project paid for with borrowed money, but the memo and the bubble talk are opinions, not proof of distress.
summary: Yahoo Finance reports, citing Bloomberg for a staff memo, that shares of CoreWeave, which rents out Nvidia chips to AI companies and pays for much of that hardware with debt, fell 15% on Wednesday 14 October, a day after venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya posted a chart of its 2032 bonds yielding about 15% and asked whether the AI buildout is creating a private credit bubble. Elon Musk, who owns X, replied "Yikes," and chief executive Mike Intrator told staff the market is acting "irrationally."
notes: Benzinga page blocked (Cloudflare). Read Yahoo Finance's own report of the same story. Reply story: Musk replied to Palihapitiya's post of Tuesday 13 October.
